newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims fell in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims fell in latest week.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department report of initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted.
Week Ended Initial Claims 4-Week Avg. Continued Claims
R-Revised, Feb 1 Initial Claims from 325,000; Feb 1 4-Week Average from 331,000; Jan 25 Continued Claims from 2,469,000 and Jan 18 from 2,468,000.
Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 339,000 in the February 8 week.
The department said initial claims for the week ended February 8 were the lowest since the July 27, 1996 week when they stood at 294,000.
The department said seven states reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended February 1, the latest period for which data are available.
Among the largest were Tennessee, with 6,239 fewer jobless claims, Texas with 5,220, North Carolina with 4,467 and Georgia with 3,151.
Tennessee reported fewer layoffs in the construction, service, apparel and transportation equipment industries. Texas had fewer layoffs in the electrical equipment, trade and service industries.
North Carolina said it had fewer layoffs in the construction, food, apparel, chemical and electrical equipment industries. Georgia had fewer layoffs in the carpet industry.
Labor said five states reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the February 1 week.
They were California, with 11,085 additional jobless claims, Iowa with 1,572, Connecticut with 1,550, New York with 1,218 and Florida with 1,079.

California said its increase was due to a return to a five-day workweek after a shorter reporting period the previous week. It also reported layoffs in the construction and food industries, and in agriculture.
Florida had layoffs in the construction, trade and service industries, and in manufacturing. New York, Connecticut and Iowa provided no reason for the pickup in claims activity.
